title: Parsing run of the codec program
statement: Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input and let $\mathrm{mode}$ be any codec mode other than the step mode. For every bit string $y$, either there exist bit strings $x,w$ and natural numbers $s,q_1,c$ such that $y=\langle x,\langle w,\mathrm{bits}(s)\rangle\rangle$, $|\mathrm{bits}(s)|\leq |\mathrm{bits}(|y|)|$, $q_1,c\leq (8W+8)(|y|+1)$, and the codec register program, started at its length-scan label with all registers zero and run with its two membership oracles on input $y$, reaches the label for halving the auxiliary counter. At that point its registers satisfy $L=|y|$, $P=2|x|+2|w|+4$, $A=2|x|+2$, $Q_1=q_1$, $Cap=c$, $Q_2=2|x|+2|w|+4$, and $S=s$; or no such encoded representation of $y$ exists, and the program, from the same initial configuration, halts with answer false. In both cases, the execution respects its configuration precondition and every register is bounded by $(8W+8)(|y|+1)$ throughout.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine on Boolean input
$y$ is an arbitrary finite bit string
caveat: The statement relies on specialized register-program, oracle, and guarded-reachability constructions, so the informal phrasing of those execution notions is necessarily compressed.
